entities.summary:
Alessandro Oliva (1407–1463) was a prominent Italian Roman Catholic cardinal who played a significant role in the Vatican's rise to prominence during the Late Middle Ages. As a member of the College of Cardinals, he participated in several key papal elections and served as an advisor to Pope Pius II.

Oliva's influence extended beyond the Vatican, as he collaborated with other powerful figures of his time, including Lorenzo Valla, a renowned humanist scholar.

The cardinal's legacy can be seen in the development of the Roman Catholic Church's institutional structure during this period. His contributions to the Church's governance and diplomacy had far-reaching consequences, shaping the course of European history for centuries to come.

In conclusion, Alessandro Oliva's impact on the Vatican and the broader religious landscape of 15th-century Europe cannot be overstated, as he embodied the complex web of alliances, rivalries, and power struggles that defined this pivotal era in human history.
